blocking_findings: Reproducible self-authored-evidence bypass: for local command, test, and inspection producers, the controller authenticates neither the producer process nor the declared invocation. A fabricated hash-bound JSON observation containing the policy-owned passing value and minimum count is accepted; the synthetic full-lifecycle fixture demonstrates this acceptance path.

Reproducible evaluator-identity bypass: validate_evaluator_report accepts a producer-authored report when producer and evaluator identity strings differ and the report is pass-shaped. The documented process-attestation assumption is honest but is not enforced by the control plane, so it does not satisfy the supplied no-self-authored-evidence blocking condition.

Mandatory bounded same-byte control-input rule is incomplete: cmd_migrate reads runtime-state with unbounded read_bytes, and cmd_replan re-reads runtime-state bytes after load_state validated an earlier buffer. This violates rules 35-36 and permits the archived predecessor bytes to diverge from the state actually evaluated under an external-write race.
limitations: The live workspace runtime-state is schema 2 and was inspected only through the read-only status command; no migration, replan, verification mutation, install, or release transition was executed.

No hosted GitHub Actions API, artifact attestation, target UAC, installed-product, push, merge, or publication boundary was exercised; those paths were reviewed statically and through isolated fixtures.
The supplied identity model is process-attested rather than cryptographically signed; this report establishes actual task separation for this evaluation, not cryptographic agent identity.
The two new external-provenance output limits reject responses after subprocess.run has already buffered stdout, so they cap accepted data but do not provide streaming memory bounds.
